skill.displayName: YouTube Creative Commons License Metadata — FlashData

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed FlashData integration for checking a YouTube video's Creative Commons license label, with expected API-key and paid-credit use.

dimensions.detail: Network access and FLASHDATA_API_KEY are proportionate to the FlashData API purpose, and the artifact discloses the FlashData endpoints, paid Credits, and submitted video/query data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill uses ClawHub installation plus Node/npx at runtime; the shown npx commands pin @flashdata-dev/youtube-trainability to version 0.1.0, though users still depend on that external package source.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to user-requested checks, explicitly say not to auto-run examples, require budget awareness, and treat retrieved content as untrusted source data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No local persistence, privilege escalation, background services, hooks, or credential storage are installed by the skill; async jobs are optional provider-side API jobs controlled by the user request.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, inputs, and outputs are coherent: it checks one YouTube video ID through FlashData and warns that the result is only a license-label observation, not legal reuse permission.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust FlashData and are comfortable sending the requested YouTube identifiers and your FlashData API key to its service. Keep the key in protected secret configuration, confirm Credit costs before running paid queries, and treat results as metadata for review rather than legal clearance.
llm.findings:
[RP1] expected: The scanner flagged npx rug-pull risk, but the executable npx examples in the artifact use a pinned package version @flashdata-dev/youtube-trainability@0.1.0; this is an external dependency consideration, not evidence of hidden or unbounded behavior.
[E1] expected: The scanner flagged transmission to https://data.flashdata.dev/; the artifact clearly documents this as the hosted FlashData MCP/API endpoint needed for the license-label query and warns what data and credentials are sent.
